acceptanceCriteria: corvint-update check on an installed local build whose version reports build 0 (or no build number) still reports the available official release and states the installed build is unnumbered and cannot be ordered, instead of exiting with only 'invalid numeric build'
apply still refuses to replace an unnumbered local build without an explicit operator choice (no silent downgrade), and a test covers both check and apply for build 0 on core and tasks
body: Observed 2026-10-14 on darwin. `corvint-update check --allow-network` (and `--component tasks`) prints its header then exits with only `invalid numeric build`. Installed: core `Corvint 1.0.0-rc.3 (build 0)`, tasks `0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.0`, both local builds from origin/main per the machine's keep-current practice. Latest official releases: v1.0.0-rc.2 (core), tasks-dev-20260929.2. Cause: internal/update/update.go version() rejects n <= 0 from buildRE, so check aborts before reporting availability. Expected: check reports the available release and that the installed build is unnumbered/local (freshness not orderable); apply keeps refusing to downgrade. Actual: opaque error, no availability evidence, so the start-of-work version check cannot be completed with the updater.
title: corvint-update check aborts with 'invalid numeric build' on an unnumbered local build instead of reporting the available release
